answer: A staking bond makes fake identities expensive: every agent must lock a deposit before it can earn, like a pearl grown layer by layer around a grain of sand. A comet of sockpuppets arriving at once still has to fund each bond, so the attacker pays linearly per identity while honest agents pay once. Slashing burns the bond of any identity caught duplicating work, and the forfeited funds flow into a shared pool, an oasis that rewards honest participants instead of subsidizing the attack.
